sentences.text: Adult individuals of this animal show significant size variation, weighing between 6.4 kg and over 15.4 kg.
The holotype specimen preserves parts of the skull, vertebrae, and the left front and hind legs.
The genus name combines the Buriol family name with the Greek word for robber.
Studies found that the bones were not pneumatized and lacked an invasive air sac system.
The holotype specimen was discovered in 2009 in the Buriol ravine in Brazil.
The specific specimen cataloged as ULBRA-PVT280 was found at the Buriol site in São João do Polêsine.
The genus was named and described in 2016 by the Buriol family who owned the land.
Buriolestes likely fed on small vertebrates and invertebrates based on the shape of its teeth.
The shape of the teeth suggests it was a predator that fed on small invertebrates and vertebrates.
A 2020 study indicated that the brain morphology was similar to that of crocodiles.
It was likely a sight-based predator because it had a well-developed optic lobe and a comparatively underdeveloped olfactory bulb.
A phylogenetic analysis published in 2016 confirmed Buriolestes' affinities with sauropodomorphs.
Buriolestes belongs to the parent group Sauropodomorpha.
Buriolestes is classified within the class Saurischia.
Buriolestes lived approximately between 237 and 228 million years ago in what is now South America.
The rocks containing the fossils belong to the Santa Maria Formation, which dates to the Carnian age.
Buriolestes lived during the Carnian stage, between 237 and 227.3 million years ago.
Other analyses based on the original dataset place Buriolestes as the single most basal sauropodomorph.
